text:
Lina Chen: Quick heads-up — I've started a thread to align on the metric/data-model changes we need for token-level latency and per-route KPIs. Want to avoid exploding cardinality when we add kernel/batch/kv labels. @eng-runtime please chime in.

Zane Pollard: +1. We need the TSV breakdown landed before the next rollout. Current dashboards show noisy route names that kill our queries.

Mike R.: Can you paste a concrete example of the metric naming + labels you're proposing?

Lina Chen: Sure — rough draft: 
```
# metric name pattern: ri.<area>.<measure>_ms
ri.runtime.token_latency_ms{route_id="r123", model="m-1.4b", kernel="fmha_v2", batch_size="8", kv_hit="true", schema_version="v2"} 12.3
ri.runtime.kv_lookup_ms{route_id="r123", kv_region="us-west-2", schema_version="v2"} 0.5
ri.runtime.kv_cache_hit_ratio{route_id="r123", model="m-1.4b", schema_version="v2"} 0.86
```
Notes: route_id should be a short stable id (not full path). kernel values must be normalized to our canonical kernel tags.

Anna S: I like keeping schema_version as a label vs embedding in the metric name. Easier to query across releases. But careful — schema_version adds cardinality as soon as we have many versions.

Theo J: Agree on route_id. We should never expose raw route paths or user IDs in metrics. For kernel, can we restrict to a small enumerated set like [fmha_v1, fmha_v2, int8_qk, int4_qk]?

Mike R.: What about kv cache behavior — storing region or host adds a lot of cardinality. We only need kv_hit boolean and maybe a hashed shard id (shard=sh1) for debugging. Don't add hostnames.

Zane Pollard: Re: token-level latency, we also should capture token_stage labels: {stage="tokenize|kv_fetch|dispatch|kernel_exec|postproc"}. But stage will multiply series by 5x — can we instead emit separate metrics like ri.runtime.latency_tokenize_ms?

Lina Chen: Good point. Two options: 1) split out stage-specific metrics with fewer labels (prefixed names), or 2) single metric with stage label. I prefer split metrics to keep label sets small. Example: 
```
ri.runtime.latency_tokenize_ms{route_id="r123", model="m-1.4b", schema_version="v2"} 0.8
ri.runtime.latency_kernel_exec_ms{route_id="r123", kernel="fmha_v2", batch_size="8", schema_version="v2"} 9.6
```
This avoids adding stage label and keeps cardinality predictable.

metrics-bot: Alert: high-cardinality metric detected in sandbox: ri.runtime.token_latency_ms with unique label values > 1200 in last 24h.

Anna S: That alert proves the point. We broke cardinality by using full route paths and model aliases. We need a migration plan and a compatibility window.

Lina Chen: Proposed migration plan: 
1) Define canonical labels and value sets (kernel, batch_size as small ints, kv_hit boolean, route_id short token).
2) Introduce schema_version label = v2 on new metrics. Old metrics remain (v1 implicit) for 30 days.
3) Update dashboards to prefer ri.runtime.latency_*_ms (v2) and keep legacy queries for rollback.
4) Add safeguards in our telemetry ingestion to drop label values that exceed whitelist or hash them to a fixed token.

Theo J: For 4) do we mean: if label value not in whitelist, emit label="other" or label_hash="<short-hash>"? I prefer label="other" for dashboards and label_hash only for debug logs.

Mike R.: Also recommend a naming convention doc snippet and a regex for label normalization: 
```
# allowed metric name regex: ^ri\.[a-z0-9_]+\.[a-z0-9_]+_ms$
# allowed label keys: route_id, model, kernel, batch_size, kv_hit, schema_version, shard
# route_id normalization: lowercase, strip non-alphanum, truncate 16 chars
```

Zane Pollard: Can we version metric names too if we want to be explicit? e.g., ri.runtime.latency_kernel_exec_ms:v2 ? I'm worried about Prometheus compatibility with colons.

Lina Chen: Don't put version in the metric name itself — use schema_version label. Keeps Prometheus idiomatic.

Anna S: Dashboard implications: Grafana panels should aggregate with label filters: sum(rate(ri.runtime.latency_kernel_exec_ms{schema_version!="v1"}[5m])) by (route_id, kernel). But we should avoid grouping by model unless requested. Default per-route KPI should be by route_id only.

Theo J: One more wrinkle — function/tool-calling variances produce high variability. We should add a label `call_type` with values {sync, async, tool} but only allow for internal debug dashboards, not high-cardinality public views.

Mike R.: Actionable checklist from my side:
- I'll prepare a canonical label whitelist and normalization functions (PR for telemetry lib).
- Add sanitization to the ingestion pipeline to collapse unknown values to "other".

Lina Chen: I'll update the dashboard templates to the new metric names and set defaults (group by route_id only). I'll also publish a short migration doc for on-call.

Anna S: Ops: we need a rollout window and a kill-switch if ingestion errors spike. Add a circuit-breaker that can revert to v1-only emission.

metrics-bot: Note: rollout checklist created: https://internal.redwood/ops/metrics-rollout/1791000000 (mock link) :white_check_mark:

Zane Pollard: Minor nit: include units in metric help text, e.g., "tokenize latency in ms". Important for new dashboards.

Lina Chen: Agreed. Also adding example queries for SLOs. Draft SLO: 95th percentile of ri.runtime.latency_kernel_exec_ms by route_id < 50ms.

Theo J: OK. If no objections I'll start rolling the normalization PR tomorrow morning and tag @eng-runtime for review.

Anna S: No objections from me. Thanks Lina — this is helpful.

Lina Chen: Thanks everyone. I'll post the migration timeline in #eng-runtime and ping when dashboards are updated. :thumbsup:
